bodyMarkdown:
## What Is the Average Australian Salary? Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you’re paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. This guide explains the standard calculation, the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, tax, and super – all in Australian English and using the latest official figures.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The most common way to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours worked per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week (the standard under the Fair Work Act). If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year

This is your gross annual salary before any deductions. The same formula works for part-time or casual roles – just use your actual weekly hours.

### What Is the Average Australian Salary?

To answer the question “what is the average australian salary”, we turn to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings report for May 2026. For full-time adult employees in ordinary time, the average weekly earnings were $2083.70. Multiplying by 52 gives an average annual salary of approximately $108,352. For all employees (including part-time and casual), total average weekly earnings were $1579.20, or about $82,118 per year.

These are **averages** across all industries and states, not medians for a specific job. Your actual pay may differ based on your occupation, experience, and location. For job-specific pay guides, see the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for most employees not covered by an award or agreement. If you are covered by a modern award, your minimum rate may be higher. Check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for details.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements. Never include casual loading in the base rate you enter into a calculator – use the checkbox to add it separately.

### Fortnightly Pay and Weekly Comparisons

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. For example, if your weekly pay is $1004.90 (minimum wage), your fortnightly gross is $2009.80. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted per annum.

### Tax: The 2026–27 Resident Rates

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% of the excess over $190,000

Additionally, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For 2026–27, the single reduction thresholds are based on the 2025–26 figures (not confirmed in this estimate), so use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate. Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included here.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your gross pay. For example, on a $59,280 salary, your employer would contribute $7,113.60 to your super fund. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Important Disclaimer

This conversion assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

To quickly convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, use the [timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator applies the standard 38-hour week and shows gross pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super.

### Summary

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time)
- National Minimum Wage: $26.44/hr, $1004.90/week
- ABS average full-time salary: ~$108,352 per year
- Tax rates 2026–27: progressive from 0% to 45% plus 2% Medicare
- Super guarantee: 12% on top, up to $270,830

For more detailed reference tables and award rates, visit the [reference tables](/data) page.
